index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure illustrates a step-by-step process of constructing a full binary tree from an initial linear plot structure through recursive branching, as part of a method called \whatif~that leverages GPT-4 to generate alternative narrative paths. The global layout consists of three sequential stages, arranged horizontally from left to right, connected by thick black arrows indicating progression. Each stage displays a tree-like structure composed of circular nodes with dark blue borders and black text labels inside, representing plot elements denoted as p₁, p₂, p₃, p₄, with superscripts indicating different branches or versions.

In the first stage, on the far left, a linear chain of four nodes is shown: p₁ at the top, followed vertically by p₂¹, then p₃¹, and finally p₄¹ at the bottom. Each node is connected to the next by a downward-pointing arrow, forming a simple vertical path. This represents the initial human-written plot, which serves as the root for subsequent expansion.

The second stage, in the middle, shows the first level of branching. The top node p₁ now splits into two child nodes: p₂¹ and p₂², each connected via a diagonal arrow from p₁. From p₂¹, the original path continues downward through p₃¹ and p₄¹. From p₂², a new branch extends downward through p₃² and p₄². This structure forms a shallow binary tree with two branches at the second level, indicating that GPT-4 has been used to generate an alternative continuation starting from p₂.

The third stage, on the far right, demonstrates further recursive branching. The node p₂¹ from the previous stage now splits into two children: p₃³ and p₃¹. From p₃³, the path continues to p₄³; from p₃¹, it continues to p₄¹. The other branch, p₂², remains unchanged, continuing through p₃² and p₄². This results in a deeper binary tree with three levels of branching, where the left subtree under p₂¹ has been expanded again, while the right subtree remains static. The overall structure is progressing toward a full binary tree, where every non-leaf node has exactly two children.

All nodes are uniformly styled as white circles with dark blue outlines and centered black text. The connections are solid black lines with filled arrowheads pointing from parent to child, clearly indicating the direction of the plot progression. The figure visually conveys the recursive nature of the \whatif~method, where each branching point introduces a new alternative narrative path generated by GPT-4, expanding the initial linear plot into a rich, multi-path story space.
